content.title: What are Method Overloading and Method Overriding?
content.description: Method Overloading and Method Overriding are two important features of Java that implement polymorphism. Overloading provides compile-time polymorphism, while overriding provides runtime polymorphism.

content.content: Method Overloading allows multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists within the same class. Method Overriding allows a child class to provide its own implementation of a method already defined in the parent class. Together, they make Java programs flexible, reusable, and easier to maintain.

content.title: Why Learn Overloading & Overriding?
content.content: These concepts are the foundation of Java polymorphism and are among the most frequently asked interview topics.
Method overloading occurs when multiple methods in the same class share the same name but have different parameter lists. The compiler determines which method to invoke based on the arguments.

content.title: Method Overloading Example
Key Rule
content.description: Overloaded methods must differ in the number, type, or order of parameters. Changing only the return type is not sufficient.

items.question: Can parameter count differ?
items.answer: Yes. Methods can have different numbers of parameters.

items.question: Can parameter types differ?
items.answer: Yes. Different parameter types create valid overloaded methods.

items.question: Can only the return type be changed?
items.answer: No. Changing only the return type causes a compilation error.

content.content: Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides its own implementation of a method already defined in its superclass. The JVM determines which version of the method to execute at runtime.

content.title: Method Overriding Example

content.content: To override a method, the subclass must use the same method name, parameter list, and compatible return type as the superclass method.

items.question: Can private methods be overridden?
items.answer: No. Private methods are not inherited.

items.question: Can static methods be overridden?
items.answer: No. Static methods are hidden rather than overridden.

items.question: Can final methods be overridden?
items.answer: No. Final methods cannot be overridden.

content.title: Runtime Polymorphism
The @Override Annotation
content.content: The @Override annotation helps the compiler verify that a method correctly overrides a superclass method.

items.question: Why use Method Overloading?
items.answer: It improves readability by allowing related operations to share the same method name.

items.question: Why use Method Overriding?
items.answer: It allows subclasses to provide specialized implementations while maintaining a common interface.

items.question: How do they improve reusability?
items.answer: Common logic can be reused while supporting different behaviors.

items.question: Why are they important in OOP?
items.answer: They are key techniques for implementing polymorphism.

content.title: Teacher Explaining a Topic
content.content: A teacher may explain the same topic differently to school students, college students, and professionals. The method name (teaching) remains the same, but the implementation changes depending on the audience. Similarly, overriding changes behavior while keeping the same method.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Nearly every Java interview includes questions on the differences between method overloading and method overriding, runtime polymorphism, @Override, inheritance, static methods, and final methods.

items.question: Can methods be overloaded by changing only the return type?
items.answer: No. The parameter list must also change.

items.question: Can private methods be overridden?
items.answer: No. Private methods are not inherited.

items.question: Can final methods be overridden?
items.answer: No. Final methods cannot be overridden.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Method overloading uses different parameter lists for compile-time polymorphism, while method overriding uses inheritance and identical method signatures for runtime polymorphism.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Overriding requires inheritance and identical method signatures.
The JVM performs dynamic method dispatch for overridden methods.
